steps.what: Establish laser machining requirements, material properties and safety constraints
Choose laser source, beam delivery, motion and extraction architecture
Draw laser machining equipment in the engineering design system {OTHER}
Set up and assess engineering simulation cases in the optical solver {OTHER}
Check optical performance, tolerances, hazards and final drawing revision
Save the checked final laser equipment design revision

tasks.design: Test reusable geometry, drawing references and solver case configurations in the engineering design system {OTHER} first. Parameter changes populate repeated geometry and case fields; the engineer chooses the architecture, checks simulation meaning and verifies the final design before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Design revisions can require repeated geometry and solver-input entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native parameter references and case configurations can remove repeated entry without choosing the laser architecture.
tasks.still_hard: Ablation behaviour, tolerances, extraction and laser hazards require engineering judgement and physical validation.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides whether the equipment will machine the actual material safely and consistently.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated drawing entry; design authority does not change.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: engineering design tools can reuse parameterised geometry and solver case definitions; this does not establish machining performance or a measured labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is equipment design through its saved checked revision; manufacturing and actual laser operation belong to their actual producers and no avoided labour is claimed for them.

The engineer supplies material, wavelength, pulse, spot, scan and tolerance values in s1-s4. Native reusable geometry requires an actual applicable component library; missing parameters and unsupported geometry are entered manually in s3. Solver assumptions and interpretation remain in s4.
Test native configuration before code. Already-linked geometry or existing solver runtime earns no saving. Only repeated entry changes; all judgement stays.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. The same-system save has a schema-minimum one percent fully retained share; s5 is the existing engineering check, not a new approval ceremony.
unknowns: How much geometry and solver setup is repeated manually?
Which machining effects require empirical trials outside the available solver?
research_questions: On actual design revisions, does parameter reuse reduce entry without hiding tolerance or model-assumption changes?

incremental.description: Maintain reusable geometry and verify solver case mappings.

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final laser equipment design, exact revision and document destination; changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: With reusable geometry and cases, gross is 30*0.40 + 15*0.30 = 16.5; subtract 1 upkeep = 15.5. If only half that repeated entry is eligible, 8.25 minus 1 = 7.25. No solver-runtime or save-click saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select, purchase and use laser cutting equipment.

steps.what: Establish actual laser cutting requirements and authorised purchase limits
Compare laser cutting equipment specifications, trials and supplier terms
outputs: selected laser cutting equipment and terms

steps.what: Enter the selected equipment and actual purchase terms
inputs: selected laser cutting equipment and terms

steps.what: Check the final purchase version, supplier, terms and delegated authority
Submit the checked equipment purchase to its actual supplier
Set up laser cutting equipment and verify physical safeguards
outputs: actual equipment setup and safeguard observations

steps.what: Operate laser cutting equipment and observe actual cuts
inputs: actual equipment setup and safeguard observations
actual workpiece and authorised operating procedure

steps.what: Troubleshoot actual laser cutting faults and verify corrections
outputs: actual fault diagnosis and correction results

steps.what: Write and check the actual equipment operation and fault record
inputs: actual fault diagnosis and correction results

steps.what: Save the checked actual equipment operation record

tasks.design: Use existing comparison fields in {PROCUREMENT} and supplier-linked purchase entries to avoid repeated specification and term entry. The engineer still evaluates cutting trials, checks the exact purchase before submission, sets up and operates the equipment, troubleshoots faults and records actual results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier specifications and selected terms can be entered again during comparison and purchase preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native comparison views and supplier-item references can reuse verified fields.
tasks.still_hard: Cut quality, laser safeguards and fault diagnosis depend on the actual equipment and material.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer judges equipment suitability and responds to unexpected physical behaviour.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated purchasing entry; equipment and spending authority stay as actually delegated.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: purchasing systems can reuse supplier-item and term fields in comparisons and purchase drafts; physical laser commissioning and fault diagnosis remain engineering work.

assumptions: This is a provisional lifecycle mix across selection, purchase and use, not a claim that each fault triggers a purchase. Reweight to the actual branch frequencies before applying savings.

Boundary includes an engineer who actually has delegated purchasing authority. If purchasing staff place the order, their work is outside the focal denominator; retain the engineer's actual requisition action instead and reweight, without claiming other-role savings.

Supplier supplies actual model, wavelength, power, pulse limits, price, currency, warranty and delivery terms; the engineer verifies and enters them in s2-s3. Use native supplier-item fields only where populated and current; missing fields and incomparable supplier documents stay manual. All suitability judgement remains in s2.

Test native configuration before code. Existing automated comparison or order population earns no saving. Physical operation, troubleshooting and actual record capture stay fully retained; the existing record check is not a new self-approval step.
Shares and reductions are provisional, not measured. The routine purchase send and record save each have one percent fully retained shares; neither supplies a saving.
unknowns: Does the engineer place purchases or only requisitions?
How often are supplier specifications already structured?
What is the actual selection-to-operation task mix?
research_questions: Does actual repeated specification and purchase-term entry justify configuring native field reuse?

incremental.description: Check supplier-field mappings and maintain the comparison configuration.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final equipment purchase including exact supplier, amount, terms and destination; changes void approval
s9 checked final equipment operation record and exact document destination; changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated comparison and purchase entry give gross 12*0.30 + 8*0.20 = 5.2; subtract 0.7 upkeep = 4.5. If only half of those entries can be reused, 2.6 minus 0.7 = 1.9. Physical work, actual notes and sends/saves have no cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Design and equipment-use decisions remain with the engineer; repeated engineering and purchasing entry can shrink.
skills_to_grow: Native parameterised drawing and solver configuration
role.ambitious_version: Nothing changes in formal decision rights; validate reduced re-entry on actual design and equipment-use cases.
